historical_references.reference: Aisha bint Abu Bakr (614-678 CE) was the third wife of Prophet Muhammad and one of his most beloved companions. She was a key figure in the early Muslim community, known for her knowledge of Hadith and her role as a teacher and leader.

Aisha bint Abu Bakr played a significant role in the Battle of the Camel (656 CE) during the First Fitna, where she led an army to support her husband, Ali, against Muawiya I. Her involvement in the battle marked a departure from the traditional feminine roles of women in Islamic society at the time.
